title: Quick Take — Frontiers of Statistics in Science and Engineering: 2035 and Beyond
description: This is a consensus report assessing where the field of statistics stands, where its most important frontiers lie, and what investments the United States needs to sustain those frontiers through 2035 and beyond. The central argument is that statistics is a generative force in science and engineering, co-producing discoveries rather than merely analyzing data after the fact. Written as AI has become dominant in research and industry, the report maintains throughout that many of the hardest open problems in AI, including interpretability, uncertainty quantification, robustness, and calibration, are fundamentally statistical problems.

title: Ch. 1 — Summary
description: Statistics is the science through which data become wisdom. Scientific and engineering progress is driven by statistical innovation, and the field continues to evolve through reciprocal interaction with scientific innovation. With the influx of computing capacity, proliferation and interoperability of data, and availability of increasingly complex modeling, the statistical landscape is shifting in ways that will transform its demands and broaden its contributions. This report illustrates the role of statistics as a key element of science and engineering progress. Recommendations in the report highlight critical areas of stewardship, capacity-building, and investment in the statistical sciences to sustain and expand the field's contributions for U.S. competitiveness. This summary presents selected key findings, conclusions, and recommendations that underscore the report's main message. (Within the body of the report, key findings, conclusions, and recommendations are numbered according to the chapter number and order of appearance. However, selected key findings, conclusions, and recommendations have been included in the Summary in the order that best preserves narrative flow, which may not align with this numbering scheme.)

title: Ch. 2 — Introduction
description: The frontiers of statistics are dynamic and constantly evolving to meet the shifting needs of science and engineering. Rooted in the pursuit of finding practical solutions to real-world challenges, the discipline brings insight and wisdom through observations and experiments. Throughout history, statistics has been a catalyst for innovation across scientific endeavors. Examples from the 20th century alone include advancement in precision agriculture that increases yields and improves efficiency of land use; pioneering design, implementation, and analysis of human clinical trials for effective and safe medical treatments; groundbreaking analyses of observational data linking the hazards of smoking and the benefits of healthy diet and exercise; and breakthroughs in statistical process control to optimize production and minimize waste in industry.

title: Ch. 3 — Statistics: A Snapshot of a Dynamic Field
description: The field of statistics is broad. Advances in the field often fall into one or more of three categories: theoretical, methodological, or applied. Individual research statisticians often seamlessly move between the categories with significant contributions across the spectrum.

title: Ch. 4 — The Changing Nature of Data
description: Data are foundational to science and engineering. The concepts and models relating to data are fundamental to the dynamic intersection of theory and application that drives innovation, refines methodologies, and provides ongoing and bidirectional links between statistics and science and engineering. The very nature of data, both in concept and in practice, is constantly evolving due to changes in measurement technology, interconnectivity, and computing power, and these changes drive the frontiers of the field of statistics.

title: Ch. 6 — Statistical Innovations That Enable New Scientific and Technological Advances
description: This chapter examines how statistical sciences facilitate scientific and technological innovation and how emerging technologies are reshaping the landscape of statistics. An earlier chapter described the life cycle of statistical innovation. Another explored how data and data collection are changing. Yet another highlighted successful examples of collaboration between statistics and domains within science and engineering. This chapter connects and expands these points by proposing that these changes in the nature of data, how data are collected, and how researchers collaborate to understand these data are both drivers and products of technological advancement. This self-reinforcing cycle also drives and, crucially, is driven by statistical advancements. The collection of the many ways statisticians explore, model, visualize, interpret, and understand data represents an inherent and crucial part of technological advancement. Such "data-driven innovation" is explicitly addressed in the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's report Data-Driven Innovation: Big Data for Growth and Well-Being.

title: Ch. 7 — Statistics Education, Training, and Workforce Development
description: As statistics enters an era shaped by the rise of artificial intelligence and progressively interconnected or interoperable data products, statisticians must critically view, evaluate, and expand the frontiers of statistics education and workforce development to support and enhance the dynamic theoretical, methodological, and collaborative frontiers detailed in the preceding chapters. Statistics must continue to modernize its talent pipeline by equipping a workforce to handle evolving data and to confront the questions that result from this evolution. At the same time, a clear need exists to expand data literacy and data acumen in the professional workforce and in the general public. Statistics is well positioned to lead these efforts and advance statistical thinking as data increasingly inform decision making in science and engineering. Such statistical thinking helps people accurately interpret, trust, and effectively employ autonomous tools based on data, algorithms, and machine learning.

title: Ch. 8 — Recommendations
description: This chapter introduces the report's recommendations and includes the supporting conclusions and key findings from throughout the report. title: Ch. 9 — Appendices
description: The National Academies will assemble an interdisciplinary ad hoc committee to produce a forward-looking assessment of the current state of the statistical sciences and emerging opportunities for the discipline and its stakeholders as they look ahead to 2035 and beyond. The study may make recommendations to funding agencies on how to adjust and expand their portfolios of activities and partnerships to reflect the evolution of the field and strengthen the impact of the discipline.
